findings.claim: The ToolbarMenu trigger's onClick now focuses the trigger for every ToolbarMenu caller, a behaviour change outside the planned `quiet` shape touch point.
findings.impact: Every ToolbarMenu user (SortMenu, ArchiveToolbar, ViewMenu, PdfPreview, the Library sort menus) now moves focus to the trigger on click. Safari and WebKit do not focus a button on click, so Escape now closes these menus there where it did not before. The change looks harmless or even helpful, but no touch point or invariant covers it, and I15 only checks drawing.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ToolbarMenu.tsx:196-201 adds `triggerRef.current?.focus()` to the shared onClick, which runs whatever the shape. The touch point lists only the `quiet` shape for ToolbarMenu.tsx. The new TargetMenu.addonKey.test.tsx sends Escape to `document.activeElement`, which seems to be why the line was added.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant breaks (I15 is about drawing), but the change reaches every ToolbarMenu caller and the touch-point list does not name it.

findings.proposed_fix: Add the focus change to the touch points (ToolbarMenu: trigger focus on click for every shape), or limit it to what the change needs.

findings.claim: An existing test, frontend/src/components/videoapp/__tests__/VideoApp.states.test.tsx, was edited even though no touch point names it.
findings.impact: The assertion moved from `findByText(/main · 0/)` to finding the drive span and checking the parent's textContent. It still checks the same text, so nothing slips through, but this existing test was edited without being planned. The spec lists the existing tests that stay unedited, and this one is not among them.
findings.evidence: VideoApp.states.test.tsx around line 374. The edit follows from AppHeader.tsx splitting the scope into a drive span and a detail span, which breaks the single text node.

bucket_proposal.reason: An edit outside the touch points that breaks no invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: List the VideoApp test that reads the scope text among the touch points.

findings.claim: frontend/src/components/readingapp/ReadingAppHeader.tsx and frontend/src/components/videoapp/VideoAppHeader.tsx are edited (doc comments on `actions`), and no touch point names them.
findings.impact: None for a user. Only comments change, and they now match the new placement of actions.
findings.evidence: In both files the `actions` JSDoc changed from 'Beside the Target button.' to 'Below the tabs on a phone, beside the Target at `sm` and wider.'

specification_compliance: Outside the implicit spec, INDEX and review paths, every other file in the diff maps to a listed touch point: DESIGN.md, the backend test, ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md, both user guides, everything under frontend/e2e-components/ (including projects.ts and spec-viewport.spec.ts), e2e-layout/fixtures/video-app.html, PageHeader.tsx, ToolbarMenu.tsx, AppHeader.tsx, TargetMenu.tsx with its new addon test, useShownTargets.ts, both LibraryControls.tsx files (which hold ReadingSortMenu and SortChoiceMenu), both shelf pages, appPrefs.ts, appTarget.ts, readingAppTarget.ts and the lib/__tests__ files.

The places outside the list are: the shared onClick focus in ToolbarMenu (R1), VideoApp.states.test.tsx (R2), componentFixtureParity.test.tsx (R3), and the comments in ReadingAppHeader.tsx and VideoAppHeader.tsx (R4).
AppHeader builds the scope from tc('driveScope', {drive: ''}).trimStart(). Both en and ja use the template '{drive} · {detail}', so the rendered text matches the old output.
potential_unspecified_behavior: ToolbarMenu now focuses its trigger on click for every caller and shape. In browsers that do not focus buttons on click (Safari), the Escape-to-close and focus behaviour of every toolbar menu changes.
regression_risks: AppHeader now builds the scope by passing an empty drive to the driveScope template and trimming. If a locale's template ever puts {drive} anywhere but first, the separator and detail will render wrong.
The video-app.spec.ts header test still measures the hand-copied fixture and was not moved to the real-component test as the touch point says. It now checks the redrawn copy, not the real AppHeader.
test_coverage: The touch point names 'PageHeader.tsx and its tests', but the diff changes no PageHeader unit test. The scopeEnd option is covered only through AppHeader in the e2e-components specs, and nothing tests I15 (other PageHeader callers unchanged) directly.
frontend/e2e-layout/video-app.spec.ts is not edited. Its header assertions were planned to move to the real-component test; they still run against the redrawn hand fixture.
not_verified: I did not run any test, unit or e2e, so I cannot say whether the suites pass.
